## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Lobha Sutta* is the opening discourse of the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 1; PTS It 1) [SuttaCentral]. In this discourse, the Buddha declares that by completely abandoning greed (*lobha*), one is guaranteed the attainment of non-return (*anāgāmitā*) [SuttaCentral]. In the Pali commentarial tradition, the *Paramatthadīpanī* (the commentary to the *Itivuttaka*) introduces the discourse with an exegesis on the honorific epithets *arahat* and *bhagavā*, and elaborates on the four foundational resolves (*adhiṭṭhāna-dhamma*): truthfulness (*sacca*), relinquishment (*cāga*), calm (*upasama*), and wisdom (*paññā*) [Boriharnwanaket]. The discourse has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Sujato under the title *Greed*, and features among 18 translations across 16 languages hosted on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include Chinese versions found in the *Itivuttaka* translation T 765 (T 765.13) and the *Ekottarāgama* (EĀ 11.1) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus's automated text-reuse analysis confirms the alignment with the *Ekottarāgama* (T 125, fascicle 6) [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies 27 matching passages across 10 texts, largely reflecting the formulaic structural reuse shared with closely related discourses in the *Itivuttaka* that treat the eradication of other defilements—including the *Dosa Sutta* (Iti 2), *Moha Sutta* (Iti 3), *Kodha Sutta* (Iti 4), *Makkha Sutta* (Iti 5), *Māna Sutta* (Iti 6), and *Lobhapariññā Sutta* (Iti 9)—as well as textual correspondences in the commentary (*Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā*) and sub-commentarial literature such as the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
